title: Where Do Embodied Decisions Come From? Rethinking Latent and Explicit Reasoning
models: in-house driving VLA: SigLIP + Qwen2.5-7B + MLP projector, three training stages (pre-aligned, AD-general, object-specific)
OpenVLA fine-tuned on LIBERO-90 with ECoT-Lite CoT annotations
Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Video-R1 (zero-shot video QA, supplementary)
action_head: discrete tokens / text outputs (driving decisions and waypoints generated autoregressively; OpenVLA discrete action tokens)
methods: inference-time CoT intervention (fixed mismatched trace; own trace with direction tokens inverted)
think-then-act (TTA) vs decide-then-explain (DTE) generation order, including TTA-trained/DTE-inference
Visual Conditional Contribution (log-prob drop when image replaced by a black frame) and Reasoning Conditional Contribution (log-prob drop when CoT content replaced by padding)
layer- and head-averaged attention ratios to visual / prompt / generated tokens
CoT quality comparison (original vs refined CoT)
question: Is an explicit chain of thought placed before the action actually driving an embodied model's decision, and is that the best place for it?
key_findings: CoT helps weak models and slightly hurts stronger ones (Table 1): navigation F1 63.73 -> 68.89 with CoT for the pre-aligned model, but 73.49 -> 72.14 for the object-specific model and 70.40 -> 69.13 for AD-general.

Intervening on the CoT under TTA collapses navigation F1 from 72.14% to 11.84% (fixed mismatched trace) and to 16.80% (own trace with direction tokens inverted); path ADE degrades only 1.83 -> 2.00 / 1.88 m (Table 2).

Decide-then-explain improves navigation F1 from 72.14 to 74.50 (hybrid training 71.71 -> 74.04) and path ADE 1.83 -> 1.80; mean VCC rises (navigation 0.25 -> 1.27; path 0.48 -> 0.62) and attention to visual tokens rises (17.96% -> 30.15%) (Tables 4-5).
A refined, more concise CoT recovers the strong model's performance under TTA (F1 73.85, ADE 1.74 vs 72.14 / 1.83 with original CoT) (Table 3).
On OpenVLA LIBERO-90: no CoT 62.0%, TTA 67.1%, DTE 69.2% success (std < 0.5%) (Table 6).
Zero-shot reordering also helps general video VLMs (e.g. Qwen2.5-VL-7B VideoMME 50.93 -> 54.51) (Table 7).

evidence.setting: both kinds of data: offline proprietary driving logs (open-loop) and LIBERO-90 simulation (closed-loop)
benchmarks: Li Auto Navigation Decision and Target Path Generation (proprietary)
evidence.scale: held-out driving test splits (sizes in appendix, not extracted); LIBERO-90 trial counts not stated in main text; reported std: +/-0.10 F1, +/-0.01 ADE/FDE, <0.5% LIBERO
evidence.statistics: partial: single std figures, no per-condition variance or tests
evidence.baselines: no-CoT, TTA, DTE, hybrid training; random/irrelevant CoT controls in appendix

causal_validation: Yes at the text level: replacing or inverting the CoT under TTA collapses decisions, showing CoT is on the causal path when placed before the action. VCC and RCC are input-ablation (black image, padded CoT) log-probability measures. The TTA vs DTE comparison changes training as well as inference, which the authors explicitly say is not a clean causal identification.
closed_loop: Mixed: driving results are open-loop on logged data; LIBERO-90 results are closed-loop success rates.
limitations_stated: 'Latent reasoning' is defined only as absence of CoT tokens, ignoring other internal representations.
TTA vs DTE differ in training and inference factorization, so the comparison is a structural probe.
critique: Agrees with 2603.12717 that text reasoning placed before the action is causally load-bearing, and adds that this can be a liability for strong models; together they show CoT is a control surface, not a passive explanation.
RCC = 0.00 under DTE is true by construction (the action precedes the CoT), so presenting it as a finding overstates the evidence; the informative result is the VCC and accuracy change.
Performance differences are small (1-2 F1 points, 0.03 m ADE, 2.1 points on LIBERO-90) and rest on a single model per domain with unspecified seeds; 'std +/-0.10' is not explained.

Under DTE the post-hoc explanation is by design a rationalization of a committed decision, which undercuts the interpretability motivation for CoT; the paper does not evaluate whether DTE explanations are faithful.
Attention ratios averaged over all layers and heads are descriptive only (the appendix notes their limits).
Mechanistic language ('latent reasoning dominates') goes beyond what input ablations and generation-order changes can show; no activation-level analysis.
one_line: Corrupting a driving VLA's chain of thought collapses its decisions (F1 72% to 12%), yet generating the action first and the explanation afterwards makes the model rely more on vision and perform slightly better in driving and on OpenVLA LIBERO-90, suggesting CoT works best as a training signal rather than an inference-time step.
